title: Creating an instance of the COM component with CLSID from the IClassFactory failed

status.label: Needs focused investigation
status.detail: PowerToys Run failed when launching Teams because COM activation of the application activation manager reported class not registered.

next_action.label: Reproduce and review proposal
next_action.reason: Current source constructs the COM activation manager before the try/catch around ActivateApplication; a registration failure at construction can escape that handler. Handling it cannot by itself repair Windows COM registration or guarantee Teams launches.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle activation-manager construction failures gracefully
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reported class-not-registered exception may arise while constructing the COM manager, outside the existing activation exception handler.
plan: Move or wrap manager construction inside the existing failure-handling boundary.
Keep the user-facing launch failure notification and diagnostic context without assuming the app was launched.
Add a test seam that simulates a COM class-not-registered construction failure and confirms no unhandled exception.
verification: A missing activation COM class produces a bounded error instead of crashing PowerToys Run; normal packaged-app launches still work.

reproduce.title: Handle activation-manager construction failures gracefully
prerequisites: Windows test environment where missing activation-manager registration can be simulated safely
setup: Use an isolated test seam rather than modifying system COM registration.
steps: Launch a packaged-app result with manager creation configured to throw 0x80040154.
Observe whether Run remains responsive and reports launch failure.
reproduce.expected_result: The launch failure is reported without an unhandled crash and successful activation still launches the app.
